About Encore Performing Arts
Empowering young artists, on stage and off
A 501(c)(3) youth theater in St. George, Utah ,  using the craft of performance to build skills that last a lifetime.
Meet the team ↓
Support Encore
Our Mission
Encore Performing Arts inspires and empowers young artists to discover and develop important life skills through unparalleled arts education, mentorship, and extraordinary theater experiences.
Through the lens of acting, storytelling, and theater-making, we help young artists grow skills that carry far beyond the stage.
Collaboration & teamwork
Critical thinking & problem-solving
Giving & receiving feedback
Communication
Confidence
Leadership
Empathy
What We Believe
Inspiring. Inclusive. Enriching.
Inspiring
We believe in the transformative power of musical theatre. Whether a student decides to work in the arts or become a doctor, lawyer, engineer, or educator, the creative and collaborative experiences they have through arts education can inspire confidence, innovation, and empathy.
Inclusive
We believe in celebrating the individuality of all people through rich artistic and social experiences. Musical-theatre-based arts education allows everyone involved to share differing perspectives and build connections across communities, backgrounds, and abilities.
Enriching
We believe learning is an eternal process, and that arts-based education allows individuals of all learning styles to grow beyond barriers and prepare for life's possibilities. By providing innovative, imaginative, and enlightening opportunities across all subject areas, Encore helps guarantee the future of our art form.

Musical Theater Camps
A whole show in a single week. Our week-long camp intensives are where our youngest Young Artists, ages 6 to 11, take their very first steps on stage, joyful, supportive, and often a family's first taste of Encore.

About Camps
Musical Theater Camps are Encore's week-long intensive format for our youngest Young Artists, ages 6 to 11, and the very first tier of our Junior Stages pathway. Inspired by classic theater camps, a full show is rehearsed and performed in about a week, with performances running around 30 minutes. The format is charming and endearing, with just enough structure to model what real theater feels like. Joy and curiosity come first.

FAQ
Camp questions
Everything families ask before a Young Artist's first camp. Don't see your question? Reach out , we're glad to help.
Who are Camps for?
Camps are designed for our youngest Young Artists, ages 6 to 11. They're the first tier of our Junior Stages pathway and a wonderful first introduction to Encore.
How long is a camp?
Camps run as a short intensive of about 6 to 8 days: Young Artists rehearse and perform a full show in that time, typically culminating in one performance of about 30 minutes.
What show will my Young Artist perform?
Each camp stages a short, age-appropriate adaptation of a licensed musical. Past camps have included Dare to Dream Camp and Jungle Book Camp. Camp adaptations are shorter and distinct from our full productions of the same titles.
Who leads the camps?
Camps are guided by Encore staff alongside counselors from our Youth Leadership Program, older, experienced Young Artists who mentor the youngest campers while developing their own teaching and leadership skills.
Does my Young Artist need experience?
Not at all. Camps are built around fun and foundational skills, with joy and curiosity first. They're often a young person's very first experience on stage.
What comes after Camps?
Camps are the entry point of the Encore pathway. The natural next step is our Junior Shows, then Emerging Artist Shows, then Signature Shows.
Ready for their first stage?
Camps are often a family's first taste of Encore. We're happy to help you find the right starting point.

Emerging Artists is where Young Artists ages 12 to 14 grow into real performers. Building on Camps and Junior Shows, this tier casts Young Artists in full licensed productions with bigger roles, sharper choreography, and deeper training, the stretch between a first taste of the stage and our most advanced work. It is the step where technique, stage presence, and responsibility all start to come together.

Emerging Artist questions
What families ask about the Emerging Artists tier. Don't see your question? Reach out , we're glad to help.
Who are Emerging Artist Shows for?
This tier is built for Young Artists ages 12 to 14 who are ready to grow, taking on bigger roles, deeper training, and full productions.
How is this different from Junior Shows?
Junior Shows are a Young Artist's first full productions, with the basics taught well. Emerging Artists raises the bar, more demanding material, sharper choreography, featured and lead roles, and more responsibility on and off stage.
Are these full productions?
Yes. Emerging Artists are cast in complete, fully staged licensed musicals with a real rehearsal process and a real run, not a short-form showcase.
Does my Young Artist need experience?
Some stage experience helps, but it isn't required. Many Emerging Artists come up through Camps and Junior Shows; others join here. Reach out and we'll help you find the right starting point.
How do auditions work?
Productions are cast by audition each season. See what's currently open on our auditions page, where dates and how to register are posted for each show.

Signature Shows
Encore's flagship productions. Full, story-driven musicals with complete production values, where rigorous artistic training meets compassionate mentorship, for Young Artists ages 13 to 18.

About Signature Shows
Signature Shows are Encore's flagship, most advanced productions, and the entry point into our Signature Stages program. Each is a full, story-driven musical with complete production values: sets, costumes, lighting, and sound, running for roughly a dozen performances. They ask for professional-level commitment while keeping the educational support that lets Young Artists take real creative risks. Staff- and faculty-led mentorship creates a safe space to discover, develop, and grow a unique voice through storytelling and the art of performance.

Our most advanced stage
Professional-level commitment, full production values, and mentorship that makes real artistic risk safe.
Full production values
Complete, story-driven musicals with real sets, costumes, lighting, and sound, running for roughly a dozen performances per production.
Professional-level training
Industry-standard rehearsal practices and expectations, paired with the educational support that lets Young Artists take real creative risks.
Mentorship and a safe space
Staff- and faculty-led mentorship throughout the process, so Young Artists can discover, develop, and grow their unique voice.
Advanced craft

Signature Shows commonly pair the production with a weekly acting class grounded in the major theorists of stage acting: Stanislavski, Meisner, Hagen, Chekhov, Linklater, Bogart, and Johnstone, applied directly to the show's actual script. FAQ
Questions about Aspire
Everything families ask about joining the show choir, auditions, and rehearsals.
What ages do you cast in Aspire?
Aspire can accommodate ages 6–18. Please note that high school graduates are not eligible to participate as a performer.
How does casting work?
Casting at Aspire is about more than talent, it’s about building well-balanced, cohesive teams where every performer can thrive. Each of our five Aspire groups is carefully curated to reflect a mix of ages, skill levels, vocal ranges, and even height when needed. Just like assembling a sports team, we consider how individual strengths come together to support the group as a whole. Being placed in a particular group is not a ranking of ability, it’s about matching each performer to the group where they can contribute meaningfully and grow confidently. No matter where you’re placed, you’re an important part of the Aspire family.
What is the cost to participate?
Tuition is typically around $395 per semester. Payment plans and limited scholarships are available to help make the program accessible to all families.
Do you offer scholarships to help cover the registration cost?
Yes. Encore and Aspire want to welcome as many young performers as possible and don’t want finances to be a barrier. We have a few scholarships available each semester, so apply early. You can apply here.
I heard you take the group on trips, is that true?
Yes. We’ve taken our groups to California, Disneyland, and on cruises to perform. There are always new performance opportunities for our groups.
What’s the difference between Aspire and other Encore programs?
Aspire is focused on vocal and show-choir-style performance rather than full musical theater productions. It includes ensemble work, choreography, and concert-style showcases.
How often does Aspire rehearse?
Rehearsals are typically held once a week during each semester, with additional rehearsals scheduled closer to performance dates.
What does the audition involve?
Auditions are relaxed and fun. Performers sing a short section of a song and learn a simple movement combination. No previous experience is required.
Is there a performance at the end of the semester?
Yes. Each Aspire group prepares a themed performance showcased at a professional venue for friends, family, and the community.
There are lots of performances scheduled, do I need to be at each one?
Yes. We ask that every performance and every rehearsal be attended by each performer.
What is Illuminate?
Illuminate is Aspire’s advanced touring ensemble. Members are selected by audition and take on more challenging material and additional performance opportunities, often including travel.
Do I need to participate in the Fall season to join Illuminate in the Spring?
It is strongly preferred that those who intend to participate in Aspire’s Illuminate Touring Company (Fall thru Spring season) participate in the Fall, including for Villains Night. If there are enough participants to fulfill the available spots for the Fall program, which there usually are, then anyone not participating in the Fall program will generally not be allowed to participate in Illuminate in the Spring. Auditions at Encore
Every season we cast young performers in fully staged musicals at the historic Electric Theater. No experience required, just bring your voice and your nerve.

How it works
Auditions
What you can audition for next
Auditions are posted here as each show opens. Nothing is casting right now.
No auditions are open at the moment. Our next casting call will be posted here, and you can hear about it first by signing up for the newsletter below.
Listings change through the year. Don't see your show yet? Sign up for the newsletter on our home page and we'll let you know the moment auditions open.
Auditioning here is less of a test and more of an invitation , a room full of people who genuinely want to see you do well.
You'll sing a little, learn a short dance, and maybe read a few lines. Our directors and choreographers coach as they go, so even if it's your very first audition, you won't be left guessing. Nerves are part of it, every performer on our stage felt them too.
We cast first-timers in every production. What we're looking for isn't polish; it's energy, effort, and the willingness to try something in front of other people. Bring that, and you're already most of the way there.
The process
How an Encore audition works
Four steps, start to finish, usually wrapped up in a single visit plus callbacks.
1Sign up & pick a timeRegister online for the show you want and choose an audition slot that fits your schedule.
2Sing for usPrepare a short song, about 30 to 60 seconds. Not sure what to bring? We'll point you in the right direction.
3Learn a danceA choreographer teaches a short combination on the spot. No dance background needed, just follow along.
4Callbacks & castingSome performers are asked to sing or read again. Then the cast list goes up and rehearsals begin.
Come prepared
What to bring
Keep it simple. Three things and a good attitude.
A song you loveAround a minute, in a key that's comfortable for you. Sheet music or a backing track helps, but isn't required.
Clothes you can move inSomething comfortable for the dance portion, plus shoes you can actually dance in.
Just yourselfCome as you are. We're looking for energy and effort, not perfection, and definitely not a polished resume.

See it for yourself

Audition questions
Do I need experience to audition?No. Encore casts first-time performers in every production, and auditions are designed to be welcoming for all experience levels.
Is there a fee to audition?There is no fee to audition. A participation fee applies once a performer is cast, and need-based scholarships are available, see our scholarship page.
What should my Young Artist prepare?A short song of about one minute in their range, and clothes they can move in for the dance portion. We will help if you are not sure what to sing.
Do we audition for a specific role?You audition for the production and the director casts roles. You can note a role you are interested in, but every performer is considered for the best fit.
When and where are auditions held?Auditions are held at the Electric Theater in downtown St. George ahead of each production. Dates are listed on each show page and announced by email.

Don't see what you're looking for? Call (435) 414-0049 or send a note and we'll help.
How much does a sensory-friendly performance cost?
Encore is proud to offer sensory-friendly performances at no cost to our patrons. Tickets are free, but they must be reserved in advance on our website.
Can I show up without a reservation?
Unfortunately we cannot accept walk-ins at this time. Tickets must be reserved in advance on our website so we can plan the right experience for every guest.
What is a sensory-friendly performance?
A sensory-friendly performance is a theater production that welcomes individuals with sensory needs, including people on the autism spectrum, as well as first-time theatergoers and young guests. The show is modified to allow for patron movement, staff and actors are trained to accommodate patron needs, and all patrons are welcome in a safe, non-judgmental environment.
Who are sensory-friendly performances for?
They're designed for individuals with sensory needs, guests on the autism spectrum, first-time theatergoers, young guests, and anyone who's more comfortable in a relaxed theater setting. Everyone is welcome.
Can we move around or leave during the show?
Yes. The show is modified to allow for patron movement. You're welcome to move, take a break in the lobby, and return whenever you're ready, in a safe and non-judgmental environment.
What if my family has a specific need?
Please call us at (435) 414-0049 before your visit. Our staff and actors are trained to accommodate patron needs, and we'll do everything we can to make your experience welcoming.
Mission & Objective
Encore aims to establish an inclusive and warm atmosphere that welcomes everyone. Through the regular introduction of sensory-friendly performances, Encore endeavors to ensure that individuals of all backgrounds and situations can attend and appreciate Encore productions ,  while also educating and equipping our staff and performers.
01
Community Advisory Committee
To enhance the experience for our patrons, Encore has established an advisory committee of knowledgeable members from the local St. George community ,  parents, teachers, caregivers, and individuals who identify as neurodiverse. We built it by reaching out to contacts in our network, consulting school drama and resource teachers for recommendations, and collaborating with local non-profits such as TURN and RRCI.
The committee attends performances and dress rehearsals to experience the show and get familiar with the venue. During these visits, they assess the production and identify anything that may need adjusting to ensure a safe, comfortable experience for patrons with sensory needs.

Creating a Sensory-Friendly Event
We invite feedback and recommendations from our advisory committee, then combine them with our own theater-specific expertise and our accessibility and inclusivity research and training.
We think about the whole experience ,  both the performance and everything around it: preparation, arrival, and navigating the space. The best events are built specifically around the show, the space, and the community.

ASL-interpreted performances
We want every story on our stage to reach every person in the room. On select performances, Encore provides American Sign Language interpretation so our Deaf and hard-of-hearing patrons can share fully in the magic of live theater.
Select performances
Deaf & hard-of-hearing welcome
What it is
Theater everyone can follow
At an ASL-interpreted performance, one or more qualified interpreters sign the show live, in view of the audience, as it unfolds on stage. The dialogue, the lyrics, and the feeling of the moment all come through ,  so Deaf and hard-of-hearing patrons experience the same story, at the same time, alongside everyone else.
Live interpretation
Qualified ASL interpreters sign the performance as it happens.
Select dates
We schedule interpreted dates on chosen productions and announce them ahead of time.
Why we do this
We believe live theater belongs to everyone. Access isn't an add-on at Encore ,  it's part of how we tell a story well. Offering ASL-interpreted performances is one of the ways we keep our doors, and our stage, open to the whole community. If interpretation would make a performance work for you or your family, we want to hear from you ,  it helps us decide where to offer it next.

1911·1930·2015·Today
More than a hundred years of live storytelling
Built in 1911 with three-foot-thick adobe walls, the Electric Theater opened as southern Utah's first motion picture house. It was also the first air-conditioned building in St. George ,  a detail that turned a hot afternoon into a destination and helped invent the local idea of a summer blockbuster.
The venue cycled through owners and identities over the next century, including a stretch in the 1930s as the Gaiety, a 2003 revival as a live music room, and a 2013 acquisition by the City of St. George that anchored a new downtown arts district. A multi-million-dollar restoration brought it back online in 2015, restoring the historic facade while modernizing the stage and the back-of-house.
Encore Performing Arts has called it home since 2021. Today the Electric Theater hosts our productions, classes, rehearsals, and community events ,  alongside other concerts, comedy nights, and gatherings the city programs throughout the year.

Questions about the Electric Theater
Practical answers about visiting, accessibility, and how Encore relates to the venue. Don't see your question here? Call us at (435) 414-0049.
Where is the Electric Theater located?
The Electric Theater is at 68 E Tabernacle Street in downtown St. George, Utah, in the city's arts district.
Who owns and operates the Electric Theater?
The Electric Theater is owned and operated by the City of St. George. Encore Performing Arts is a tenant ,  we perform, rehearse, and hold classes here, but the venue itself is a city facility. For events at the Electric Theater that aren't Encore productions, contact the City of St. George at (435) 627-4515.
Is the Electric Theater wheelchair accessible?
The classrooms and gallery have accessible entry, and the main theater is on the ground floor. There is no elevator access to the balcony level. Wheelchair-accessible restrooms are on the main floor, baby changing stations are in both restrooms, and a gender-neutral bathroom is at the far end of the gallery. A private nursing space is available on request.
How do I get tickets to a show?
For Encore productions, visit encorepa.org/tickets. For other events at the Electric Theater, contact the City of St. George at (435) 627-4515.
Does Encore offer sensory-friendly or ASL-interpreted performances?
Yes. Encore regularly offers sensory-friendly performances and select ASL-interpreted shows. Details vary by production ,  check the individual show page or learn more about our accessibility programs.
How old is the Electric Theater?
The building was constructed in 1911 by Charlie Whipple, Johnnie Pymm, and Sherman Hardy. It was the first motion picture theater in southern Utah and the first air-conditioned building in St. George.
Is there parking?
Free public parking is available throughout downtown St. George, including street parking on Tabernacle Street and nearby city lots. The new parking garage directly behind the Electric Theater is a great option as well. We recommend arriving 15 minutes early on popular show nights.

Participation Fees
Participation fees
Every Encore production and camp carries a participation fee. It is what makes a fully staged, professionally supported experience possible for each Young Artist ,  and we work hard to keep cost from ever standing in the way of a Young Artist who wants to be on stage.
See current shows & fees →
Apply for a scholarship
What the fee supports
A participation fee helps cover the real costs of putting on a licensed production: show licensing and scripts, costumes, sets and props, music and choreography, rehearsal and performance space at the Electric Theater, and the directors, music directors, and stage managers who mentor each cast.
Each show lists its own fee
Fees vary by program ,  a week-long camp is different from a full Signature Series production. The exact participation fee for each show is shown on that show's audition page, so you always know the cost before you register. Browse what's casting now →
Multi-Young-Artist discount
Families with more than one Young Artist enrolled receive a discount. If you have multiple performers joining a production or camp, reach out and we'll make sure the discount is applied. Contact us →
Scholarships
Cost should never be the reason a Young Artist cannot take the stage. Need-based scholarships are available for every program, and the application is simple and confidential. Apply for a scholarship →
Good to know
Participation fees are non-refundable, since costs like licensing and costumes are committed as soon as a cast is set. If you have any questions about fees, discounts, or payment, we're glad to help ,  just get in touch or call (435) 414-0049.
